correctness.rationale: The inverse-conjugacy equations imply a metric-span isomorphism; star distance rigidity yields exactly the three moving-hub types. All other classes are leaf cycle/path profiles with or without an added fixed hub, except the singleton fusion. Their labeled class sizes follow from factorial orbit counts. Formal multiset products, telescoping at \(z=1\), and the unique maximal-support profile prove the class-rank formula, two-colored partition count and sharp fixed-rank stabilization. Direct enumeration of actual conjugation equations, class-size multisets (one to four leaves), partition series (through twelve leaves), and rank jumps (ranks one to five) passes. No finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The published star-monoid element decomposition and the published \(\mathcal I_m\) cycle-chain conjugacy criterion are credited. The new joint star-specific metric-span class classification, three hub-moving types with class sizes, exact rank polynomial and sharp fixed-rank stabilization are not stated in the inspected primary papers or found in the indexed searches. This is priority conditional on the inspected evidence, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed or differently named specialized star-conjugacy calculation may contain the same formula.

The 2018 ambient conjugacy theorem and the 2022 star decomposition provide substantial ingredients; the new insight is the exact metric-star refinement, class sizes and sharp stability, not the partition series in isolation.

value.rationale: A complete class-by-class size and rank classification for a canonical inverse-semigroup equivalence is a natural exact invariant, and the sharp \(m=2r\) stabilization is a meaningful structural law across an infinite family. The hub-controlled fusion/splitting distinguishes this monoid from its symmetric-inverse-monoid components. The theorem is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a claim that a known partition sequence is new.
